Definition: from G1909 and G2065; to ask for, i.e. inquire, seek:--ask (after, questions), demand, desire, question.
BiblicalUsage: Eperotao means to ask, to inquire, to demand an answer — and the Gospels are full of it. The boy Jesus is found in the temple asking questions; the rich young ruler runs up asking what he must do; the Pharisees ask to trap Him; and Paul says God was found by those who asked not for Him.
TheologicalSignificance: Questions brought to Jesus honestly are never wasted, even when the answer costs everything. I believe the asking matters more than I used to think: the boy in the temple, the ruler on the road, and the Pharisees with their traps all found that Jesus answers questions with truth, not flattery.
RelatedEvents: The Boy Jesus in the Temple; The Rich Young Ruler
